thread:
Alex Chen: Proposal: start retaining full request bodies for only 1% of high-volume tenants, keep 30d hashed metadata for all, and surface sampled counts in console. Goal: reduce storage/cost and PII risk while keeping debuggability.
Priya Nair: +1 on reducing retention, but how do we pick the 1%? per-tenant quota? adaptive by error rate?
Sam Ortiz: We should bias sampling towards error traces and spikes. If a tenant hits anomaly thresholds, temporarily bump their sampling rate to 100% for 1h.
Jordan Li: Concern: console currently shows clickable snippets for sampled logs. We must ensure UI never shows raw body for >1% unless explicitly allowed by legal.
Maya Patel: Agree. Also need a breakglass flow for SRE/Support with audit trail. Maybe short-lived temp tokens that expire after 4 hours.
Alex Chen: Rough config draft: 
```json
{"retention": {"full_body_sample_rate": 0.01, "hash_meta_days": 30, "error_backoff_window_s": 3600, "breakglass_ttl_h": 4}}
```
Sam Ortiz: That looks fine. Also add `min_sample_per_day` to avoid losing low-volume tenants entirely. set to 1?
Priya Nair: For telemetry, we can expose aggregate counts: sampled_count, sample_rate, error_weighted_rate. No raw text in metrics. Dashboards only use metrics.
Jordan Li: UX ask: Console should clearly show when data is redacted and why. Big red banner + reason code (e.g., PII_POLICY, QUOTA_SCRUB).
Maya Patel: Ops: will audit logs capture the breakglass justification and approver id? we need that for compliance.
ops-bot: FYI: any breakglass token use will emit `breakglass.audit` event with fields [user, tenant, reason_code, token_id]. No payload captured.
Alex Chen: Good. Remaining debate: do we allow tenant-level override via support request? Legal says must be explicit consent and documented.
Sam Ortiz: Implementation detail: sampling should run in the mux layer before payload storage. That avoids storing then deleting.
Priya Nair: Can we implement a lightweight deterministic hash on tenant+request-id to select the 1%? That makes debugging repeatable.
Jordan Li: Deterministic helps, but remember to salt hashes per-tenant to avoid cross-tenant correlation.
Maya Patel: One more: add a canary rollout - enable for 5% of tenants tomorrow, monitor cost/sla/PII alerts for 48h, then widen.
Alex Chen: Plan: I'll open RFC with these configs + canary playbook. Action items: Priya to write telemetry metrics list, Sam to spec sampling hook in mux, Maya to draft breakglass audit schema.
Priya Nair: On it.
Sam Ortiz: I'll prototype the mux hook this week.
Maya Patel: I'll coordinate with legal for consent template.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: sampling-mux-proto -> canary-5pct at 2026-03-23T02:00:00Z
Alex Chen: Thanks all. If anyone sees edge cases (attachments, embeddings), drop them here.
Priya Nair: Note: embeddings are treated separately — we'll need obfuscation at vector-ingest. Adding to RFC.
Jordan Li: Also flag: mobile SDKs sometimes inline files in body; need file-size cutoff to force immediate scrub.
Alex Chen: Good catch. Will add file-size rule (<= 16KB allowed, else scrub).
